item.title: China warns Philippines over Ren'ai Reef provocation
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
China Coast Guard has warned the Philippines to cease conducting infringing provocations and stop making false narratives, its spokesman said in a statement on Thursday night. Jiang Lue said Philippine Coast Guard vessel 4409 approached waters near Ren'ai Reef to collect an injured crew member from an illegally "grounded" ship there. For humanitarian reasons, China promptly allowed the Philippines to use small boats for the transfer. China Coast Guard handled the situation in accordance with the law and provided necessary assistance, Jiang said. "However, the statements from the Philippine side disregard the facts and distort the truth, attempting to mislead public opinion," he said. "China holds indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha Islands, including Ren'ai Reef, and the surrounding waters. We sternly warn the Philippine side to immediately cease their infringing provocations and false narratives."

item.title: UNISFA Force Commander inspects 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to Abyei
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
By Zhang Zhikang, Yang Biao, Tan Chaobo, Cao Yang, Gu Chong and Zhang Xuhao Honor guard members of the 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to Abyei report to the UNISFA Force Commander. The UNISFA Force Commander reviews the honor guard of the 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to Abyei. ABYEI, Oct. 8 -- Lieutenant General Ganesh Kumar Shrestha , Acting Head of Mission and Force Commander of the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei (UNISFA), recently inspected and reviewed the 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to UNISFA. He spoke highly of the Chinese peacekeepers' conduct and discipline, combat readiness, capability to fulfill mandated tasks, and emergency response capabilities, expressing gratitude for the force's contributions since its deployment to the mission area. Members of the 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to Abyei brief the UNISFA Force Commander on anti-drone capability building. The UNISFA Force Commander inspects portable anti-drone equipment of the 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to Abyei. The UNISFA Force Commander poses for a group photo with members of the 3rd Chinese Peacekeeping Quick Reaction Force to Abyei.

item.title: Chinese Naval Hospital Ship Auspicious Ark Provides Medical Services in Guinea
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
By Zhang Yao, Wang Xuemeng, Cai Ye, Zhou Jianlong, Liu Xiaoyu, Zhang Yazhongjian, Zhang Qi, Ye Duoduo, Cao Pengfei, Ou Tan Wenjun and Wu Qiuhan CONAKRY, Oct. 8 -- The Chinese PLA Navy's hospital ship Auspicious Ark (Hull 868) has been conducting a series of activities, including medical services and cultural exchanges, during its visit to Guinea, providing medical treatment to more than 4,000 patients. On October 6, 2026, Guinean Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah visited the hospital ship, writing in the guestbook to express his gratitude and best wishes to the Chinese PLA Navy's hospital ship. The hospital ship Auspicious Ark, carrying out Mission Harmony-2026, arrived in Conakry, the capital of Guinea, on October 3, 2026, to begin a seven-day friendly visit and provide medical services, marking the first visit by the Chinese PLA Navy's hospital ship to Guinea. China and Guinea established diplomatic relations on October 4, 1959. Guinea was the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to establish diplomatic ties with China.

item.title: Japan urged to severely punish perpetrator of Chinese embassy break-in
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
BEIJING, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- China once again urges the Japanese side to impose severe punishment on the perpetrator who broke into the Chinese Embassy in Japan with a knife to serve as a warning to others, foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Thursday. Mao made the remarks at a regular media briefing while answering a question regarding the first court hearing in the trial of Kodai Murata, a former Japan Self-Defense Forces (SDF) officer accused of forcibly entering the Chinese Embassy in Japan. It is an egregious incident unprecedented in the international community that an active-duty officer of Japan's SDF broke into the Chinese Embassy in Japan with a knife and made violent threats against Chinese diplomatic personnel, Mao said. She said it constitutes a serious violation of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, poses grave threats to the personal safety of Chinese diplomatic staff and the security of the diplomatic premises, and lays bare a host of deep-seated problems in Japan, including rampant right-wing forces and inadequate management and discipline of SDF personnel. "Whether Japan can handle the case seriously in accordance with law will test whether the Japanese government earnestly fulfills its obligations under international law, and bears on the country's national credibility and international image," Mao said.

item.title: China firmly opposes U.S. arms sales to China's Taiwan region
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-07
BEIJING, Oct. 6 (Xinhua) -- China remains firmly opposed to U.S. arms sales to China's Taiwan region, Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday, stressing that the country's position is clear. Guo made the remarks in response to media reports that Taiwan recently received two F-16V fighter jets purchased from the United States and plans to receive another 64 within the year. Guo said the U.S. side needs to implement the important common understandings reached at the meeting between the two countries' presidents, abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiques, and act prudently on the Taiwan question. "The Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and resolving it is a matter for the Chinese ourselves that brooks no external interference," he said.
